messages:
nina: FYI I merged Salem's LoRA adapter into adapters/salem and kicked off a small quickpack to check int4 behavior (qp/salem_small). Seeing intermittent truncation of fractional cents and occasional dropped trailing zeros in identifiers. Anyone able to look?

omar: Can you paste a reproducible snippet?

nina: Repro: 
Order:
- ID: 001200, price: $3.20
- ID: 001201, price: $4.00
Prompt: "Return JSON with id (string) and price (string)"
Bad output: [{"id":"1200","price":"3"},{"id":"1201","price":"4"}] (dropped leading zero and .20 / .00)

omar: Quickpack summary: fp16 baseline cents_drop 0.05%, id_zero_loss 0.02%. int8 cents_drop 0.4%. int4 (symmetric) cents_drop 2.1%, id_zero_loss 1.4%.

raj: Two quick checks: 1) adapter-level normalization that strips leading zeros? 2) tokenizer splitting behavior for dot+digits.

nina: Adapter had a normalization hook for legacy IDs. I removed it and re-ran: id_zero_loss down to 0.3% but cents_drop stayed ~1.7%.

raj: Could be quant scale clipping in int4 symmetric mode. Try asymmetric quant or increase per-channel scale, plus add 40 targeted assertion cases in quickpack for ".00/.20/.50".

eval-bot: quickpack run qp-3571239999-a finished. Top deltas vs fp16: cents_preservation regression +1.6%, id_leading_zero_loss +0.28%, json_validity fails +0.9%.

omar: Run options: (A) int4 asymmetric, (B) int4 with per-head scales, (C) reduce prune if sparsity enabled. Also test cold vs warm KV cache — some kernels behave differently on early tokens.

nina: I'll push a patched quickpack (40 assertions) and run int4 asymmetric + per-head scale 0.14. If results don't hit parity we'll route Salem traffic to int8-canary.

raj: If you can isolate 8 failing examples and a tiny model snapshot we can open a runtime bug. Otherwise fallback routing is fine.

nina: Thanks all. Will post new numbers in this thread.

omarm: :thumbsup: keeping an eye on cost impact if we route to int8.
